exposure: nationality (Lebanese, Syrian, Palestinian, other migrant women)
cohort: 17,624 women giving birth at Rafik Hariri University Hospital in Beirut, Lebanon between January 2011 and July 2018
finding: Syrian refugees in Lebanon had similar obstetric outcomes compared to Lebanese women, except for a higher rate of very preterm birth, while Palestinian and other migrant women experienced worse pregnancy complications compared to Lebanese women.
mod_finding: The majority of women in the study had a caesarean section (73%).
